title: Enhancement of hydrogen spillover onto carbon nanotubes with defect feature
material_description: as-prepared | As-prepared multi-walled carbon nanotubes from catalytic decomposition of acetylene over Co0.05Mg0.95O at 973 K; 5-15 nm tube diameter by HRTEM; no KOH activation, no cobalt loading
purification_method: 37% HCl immersion, de-ionised water wash, dried at 373 K; stated purity above 90%
notes: Chen & Huang 2008. THE MEASUREMENT IS NOT ISOTHERMAL, and that is the single most important thing about these rows. The reported quantity is a weight difference across a 303 -> 673 -> 303 K cycle at ambient pressure in flowing hydrogen at 20 mL/min: the 303 K end of the cooling branch (adsorbed) against the 673 K end of the heating branch (desorbed). Nothing is measured at a single temperature and there is no vacuum or zero-coverage baseline -- the reference state is a sample at 673 K still sitting in 1 atm of hydrogen. So measurement_mode is temperature_cycle, temperature_k 303 is the adsorption state and reference_temperature_k 673 the desorption reference. THESE VALUES ARE NOT COMMENSURABLE WITH AN ISOTHERMAL UPTAKE AT 303 K and must be excluded from Chahine plots and isotherm fits, for three independent reasons: the reference state still holds whatever hydrogen is bound at 673 K, so the swing is a lower bound on true 303 K loading by an unknown amount; it is a 5 K/min dynamic ramp, not an equilibrated state at either end; and the paper assumes the whole weight change is hydrogen, so any residual cobalt reduction, decomposition or uncorrected buoyancy enters as uptake. The gas is FLOWING, not a static charge, which measurement_mode cannot also record; 1.01325 bar is nominal ambient, not a measured pressure. Cobalt appears in two distinct roles and two distinct fields: metal_loading_wt_pct is the intentional impregnation measured by AAS (Table 2), residual_metal_wt_pct is leftover synthesis catalyst from the Co0.05Mg0.95O growth catalyst (Table 1). The paper never calls Co a dopant and reports it in weight percent, so dopant_element and dopant_concentration_at_pct stay empty. No surface area is reported for ANY cobalt-loaded sample. Neither 'excess' nor 'absolute' occurs; the four 'excess' hits are all 'excessive' describing defect sites. 'Total' occurs in Eq. (1) and Eq. (3) as 'total H atoms uptake' and 'total H2 capacity', but there it means catalyst plus support summed in the spillover decomposition, not a thermodynamic basis, so uptake_type stays unspecified. Apparatus: Cahn TG2121 thermogravimetric analyser, 10 mg sample, quartz blank correction under the identical thermal program, explicit buoyancy correction, UHP H2 99.9995% through a moisture trap, runs repeated at least once. No leak test and no calibration standard. TWO INTERNAL PROBLEMS THE VERIFICATION FOUND, recorded rather than resolved. First, the paper's own H/Co and enhancement-factor columns are arithmetically inconsistent with its as-prepared series: taking the stated 0.22 wt% baseline, Eqs. (2)-(3) give enhancement factors of 2.16 to 5.05 where Table 2 prints 0.97 to 2.54, implying a baseline of 0.33 to 0.49 rather than 0.22. The 973 K series reproduces cleanly. Second, the paper's own spillover criteria fail for the lowest as-prepared loading while the text asserts spillover generally: it says the atom ratio is 'larger than one' and that the enhancement factor 'should be greater than one', and that row's values are 0.69 and 0.97. H/Co and the enhancement factor have no schema fields. Traps: the enhancement-factor column (0.97-3.25) is dimensionless and sits in the same table and the same numeric range as the wt% uptakes, with 3.25 printed beside an uptake of 3.41; H/Co runs 0.69-37.88; the Co0.05Mg0.95O growth-catalyst stoichiometry collides with the 0.05 M impregnation label; 973 K is both the nanotube synthesis temperature and an activation temperature; the TG sample is 10 mg while the impregnation batch is 100 mg. §13.3: BET 2, method 2, T/P 0 (the conditions are a cycle, not a state), uptake type 0, purity 1, calibration 1, Chahine 0 (not assessable for a temperature-cycle swing) = 6 -> Tier B. RECONCILIATION (agent C, 2026-11-09): free_volume_calibration left empty: the H2 measurement is gravimetric (TG) and the paper describes a quartz-blank buoyancy correction, not a free-volume calibration; that correction is coded by calibration_described = true.
